tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(mission): validate repoRoot/missionID/delegationID in DisclaimDelegationRecord (PR #509 review finding)

DisclaimDelegationRecord called DelegationDir without checking its
three identifying inputs for empty, unlike its sibling filesystem
writers (WriteDelegationSkeleton, CloseDelegationSkeleton). An empty
repoRoot collapses RepoStatePath's filepath.Join to a path relative to
the process's cwd instead of erroring - on the disclaim path, which
permanently relaxes Abandon's delegation gate, that is the worst
outcome available on this branch.

Add the same three TrimSpace-empty guards the sibling functions use,
each with a field-named error. New test starts red against pre-fix
code (asserts on "repoRoot"/"missionID"/"delegationID" in the error;
pre-fix, all three land on the callee's generic "not found" message
because the path was still built and probed) and green after.

Swept the rest of this PR's delegation/pending-dispatch surface
(DisclaimDelegation, ClassifyPendingDispatches, WriteDispatchPending,
ClearDispatchPending, ConsumeDispatchPending): Store.DisclaimDelegation
already guards repoRoot/missionID/delegationID before it would ever
reach DisclaimDelegationRecord (mission-not-found / delegation-lock
errors fire first), and every dispatch-pending path already collapses
through dispatchPendingRoot/DispatchPendingPath, which return "" on an
empty input and are documented no-ops rather than wrong-tree writes -
no further gaps found.

No CHANGELOG/DES-076 entry: this hardens an already-unreachable-from-
production-callers path (defense in depth on an exported function),
not a change in observable behavior for any operator-facing flow.
EOF
)"
